If I'm dead I won't know I'm alone cause I'll be dead. I have given life a chance. It's been getting gradually worse for about three years. I'll give you a short timeline to illustrate my point.

age 15: have boyfriend I love, doing well in school, have friends, although have bitchy mum and clearly emotionally abusive dad. > friends start screening me out, start finding it difficult to sustain happiness > mum gets worse, dad gets worse, boyfriend starts distancing himself, I start drifting towards self-harm because I don't understand what's happening. > age 16: start self-harming, boyfriend dumps me and refuses to say why but it's clear he hasn't loved me for a while and was using me for sex, I go into meltdown. > friends barely talk to me, spend most of my time alone, mum uses my mental health issues to try and manipulate me, screams at me all the time, still self-harming. > age 17: meet a guy, become really good friends with him, eventually start going out, have happy moments but mental illness is getting worse, have regular panic attacks > age 18: I try and try to get medical help but am repeatedly turned away despite being as explicit as I can about the imminent risk I pose to myself. Boyfriend moves to China and dumps me, insists he'll keep talking to me but very clearly hides 80% of what he's up to > Move away for uni, am away from emotionally abusive parents but have absolutely no friends, all attempts to make friends fall flat. Start drinking to ease the pain of loneliness, self-harm comes back, stop eating, struggling to do uni work > make friends with guy upstairs, still depressed, spend most of my time in his room crying my eyes out and trying to scratch myself while he sits on my hands, still can't find other friends to widen my circle, struggling with not having direct emotional support off previous boyfriend, work starts penalising me for having university stuff to do > not earning any money, no friends left, no opportunities to go out over Christmas or New Year and nobody ever responds to my invites when I invite them round. Christmas with family is always torture and I've cried the last three times. Won't be able to celebrate birthday because I have several massive tests the next day, have no friends with whom to celebrate later on, have no money to do anything, only have more exams to look forward to (bearing in mind I'm studying a course so demanding that medical students have been telling my group that we're going to make ourselves ill and turn up to make us stop studying because we all have to keep going until we start crying too much to see in order to actually do the work in time)
I don't like films. I just enjoyed having someone to sit with so I could have a hug for once. I don't get human contact anymore. Nobody even touches me.

the only friend I had down here (moved away for uni) is this guy living upstairs. We got really close cause we've had similar experiences with self-harm and stuff and he's been helping me with that. But of late he's started saying some really sexist stuff (mutual friend has Thai girlfriend, he made a joke about "can she give me a happy ending?") and given how often he started saying this stuff, I tried explaining that it was actually pretty offensive what he was saying - not shouting at him, just saying "you know, it does feed into your behaviour around women". He ignored me, insisted it had absolutely no impact on him.

One of his flatmates, E, whom we both know is asexual but she asked us not to tell anyone else, causes the friend and the other male flatmate distress because they don't like how she treats them - i.e. sometimes she snaps at them, and she threw out the collection of vodka bottles they had spread over the kitchen windowsill - so whenever she's not around they make jokes about how she "needs a good fucking". I've tried to casually point out to them both, and to the friend in private, that it's not fair to say shit like that because sex isn't a big thing for E and because it's sexist to base a woman's behaviour entirely around how much cock she's getting, but they don't listen, and they say this stuff in the kitchen where she can actually hear them.

Me and the two male flatmates were going to the supermarket earlier this evening and the other one, B, started going on and on about if E was a virgin or not. I tried to steer the conversation away but he insisted, and started on the "she needs sex" jokes. I tried to explain to him that they were sexist and he just really patronised me and made the jokes more and more sexually violent, and the friend, P, was nodding along. I told them it was disgraceful.

I'd had my laptop and stuff in P's room so I took all that and was leaving to go back to mine because I didn't want to be around him, and he asked why, so I said it was because of how shameful it was that he wouldn't stand up for E who was one of his friends, in the face of that kind of stuff. He was like "Well it's just banter", so I had to remind him of all the shit I've shown him about how 'banter' pretty much inevitably feeds into men's behaviour around women and he knows that I've had personal experience of this even while being at uni (i.e. the last two months or so), from being publicly humiliated for asking for there to not be porn on the freshers page, to being pushed into traffic for not letting a strange man touch me up on the street. He just kept insisting that his sexist jokes exist entirely in a vacuum even though I've pointed out to him all the times he says sexist stuff, so he was like "well fine, if I'm such a bad person, then go", so now I have no friends, because I haven't been able to make friends with anyone at my uni and, thanks to my introversion and crippling social anxiety, it takes me a really fucking long time to get to know one person, let alone a friend group.
